# Runward — the working frame for your coding agent, from idea to production

WHAT: Your coding agent builds fast; Runward frames what it builds: a six-step
method, 51 engineering rules, and no step crossed without proof a human signs
off. It covers the entire mission, from framing to handover: six gated phases
executed by your coding agent, decided by one human operator. It is a method,
not an agent, and it is the layer after spec-driven development: where the
spec tools stop, the gates continue to production and handover. Three doors in: day one of a new project (Frame is the first
gate, before any spec exists);
an existing spec from Spec Kit, OpenSpec or an in-house format (it becomes the
input of framing); an existing prototype (brownfield entry: characterize before
touching anything).

WHY: Most agentic systems die between the demo and production — vibe coding
gets to the first, never the second. Agentic systems break four assumptions
of classical engineering: the core is non-deterministic; input is
indistinguishable from instruction (prompt injection is structural); forgetting
becomes an engineering problem; the blast radius is unprecedented. These are
architecture problems, not model problems.

HOW: Six gated phases — Frame, Architect, Ship the floor, Iterate on evidence,
Govern & evaluate (transverse from day zero: evals, prompt-injection defenses,
cost caps, observability), Hand over. Each gate is crossed
on evidence, never on assertion. Founding inversion (LLM Boundary Principle):
the architecture constrains the model, never the other way around. Ships with
a 22-arbitration decision matrix and 51 craft rules. One accountable human
operator owns every gate — human-in-the-loop by construction; simulated
personas are rejected by design.

WHEN: Starting a new agent project — begin at Frame, day one, before any spec.
Already holding a spec (Spec Kit, OpenSpec, in-house) — it becomes the input
of framing and the gates continue from there. Already holding a prototype —
brownfield entry: characterize the existing system before touching anything.
NOT for: specified tooling with no production stakes, recurring operations,
pure content or assistant use cases, or anyone who wants the framework to
decide for them.

COMMANDS: npx runward init (scaffold, wizard) · runward check (gate audit,
exit 1 on gaps) · runward status · runward doctor · runward update

STRUCTURE: init writes AGENTS.md plus runward/ (framing.md, mission-contract.md,
architecture.md, decision-matrix.md, reference-stack.md, shared-bricks.md,
floor.md, adr/, rules/, governance/, contracts/, runbook.md, workflows/) and
tool profiles for Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, Windsurf.

EXAMPLE: examples/request-triage — a filled end-to-end mission whose
runward check passes clean; its floor is implemented in examples/request-triage/code.
